notes: Independently confirmed the extraordinary claim that Rep. Chuck Edwards was found by the House Ethics Committee to have engaged in misconduct and was censured: fetched Blue Ridge Public Radio's original report (25-page investigation, 'persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct,' the 'lavish' gifts and 'intimate dinners and vacations' language, both staffers leaving his office, and both quoted responses) and confirmed it is a real, live article, not a Wikipedia/Ballotpedia summary.

Independently confirmed the House censure vote itself on clerk.house.gov: Roll Call 292 (119th Congress, 2nd Session), H. Res. 1498, 'In the matter of allegations relating to Representative Chuck Edwards,' passed September 1, 2026 by 413 Yea - 2 Nay. The file previously asserted 'The full House voted to censure Edwards' citing only the BPR article (s2), which was published August 3, 2026 - before the vote occurred and therefore could not support that sentence. Corrected: split that claim into its own context item and cited the official Clerk of the House roll call (added as source s9), including the exact date and vote count.

Corrected: the claim that Edwards ended his campaign on August 5, 2026 and that state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom was chosen to replace him was cited only to Ballotpedia (s1, which shows Edwards 'did not make the ballot' but gives no date or process) and the pre-dated BPR article (s2). Fetched The Epoch Times' report (confirmed via a live news search, not Ballotpedia), which independently confirms Edwards announced his withdrawal on X on August 5, 2026 and that the 11th District GOP executive committee selected Balkcom on August 10, 2026; added as source s10 and cited alongside s1/s2. Corrected the file's vaguer 'North Carolina Republican Party selected' to the more precise 'the 11th District Republican Party executive committee.'

Verified the general-election slate (Ager D, Balkcom R, Groo L; Edwards excluded as not on the ballot) against Ballotpedia's North Carolina House elections overview page, and Ager's five-way Democratic primary win (March 3, 2026, defeating Briarwood, Hudspeth, Maddox, and Whipple) against the same page.
Verified Ager's background, priorities, and quotes ('Rising costs hurt our businesses...', 'Helping the rich get richer...') verbatim against his Ballotpedia profile and campaign-ad quote.

Verified Balkcom's background (Henderson County native, East Henderson HS, Blue Ridge Community College 2016, mortgage loan officer, NC House District 117 since 2023, committee assignments) and her Candidate Connection survey quotes (HB 805, farmland-protection priorities) verbatim against her Ballotpedia profile and survey response, and her campaign-ad quote ('Protecting family farms is personal to me...') against Ager's Ballotpedia page, which hosts both candidates' ad quotes.

Verified Travis Groo's background (University of West Florida 2000, transportation profession) and survey quotes ('Balance the budget. Get rid of the income tax...', 'Property Rights.') verbatim against his Ballotpedia profile and survey response. No further corrections needed.
